inputs.original_text: Micheál Martin is pointing to more housing tenancies while the number of people in emergency accommodation has increased again and eviction notices are causing concern. That is no success story: a government can boast about leases, but families need homes they can actually keep. Forcing landlords to provide six-year leases from March 1 may sound protective, yet rules that make renting harder can leave ordinary people with fewer choices. The test is whether people have secure homes—not whether ministers can point to a headline figure.
inputs.modified_text: More tenancies mean little if people are still ending up in emergency accommodation and families are worried about eviction. Micheál Martin can point to lease figures, but security is what matters. Forcing landlords into six-year leases from March 1 may sound compassionate, yet piling on rules risks driving ordinary providers out and leaving renters with fewer options. Government should focus on stable homes for families, not headline numbers and policies that make the housing market harder to navigate.
